title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements
abstract: arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. translated_title: 开放世界AI：三个要求的故事
translated_abstract: 封闭世界要求AI具备专门化的能力，并允许它制造其理论所假设的独立同分布数据：一个固定的准则许可不断收集样本，直到任务被覆盖为止。开放世界要求的则是多面性——让机器承担它并非为此设计的任务，仅凭少量样本学习，且人类设计者几乎不提供先验——同时提供的是成组而非打乱的数据。由于任务无法预先知晓，机器必须在推理时进行学习（第一个要求）。通过将任务建模为共享潜在因子并分解训练目标，我们推导出另外两个要求：一是*丰富的表征*，它保留的信息超出独立同分布泛化所需的程度；二是预测性解耦，将输入和输出对齐为相互匹配的低维分组。该分析进一步预测需要一个一致的内部学习器，以及跨越相关任务的长上下文所带来的益处。我们在高达8B参数的语言模型上检验这些主张，探究是否……
tldr: 本文从理论上推导出开放世界AI的三个要求——推理时学习、丰富的表征以及预测性解耦，并在高达8B参数的语言模型上对这些主张进行了验证。
en_tdlr: The paper derives three requirements for open-world AI—inference-time learning, a rich representation, and predictive disentanglement—and validates these claims on language models up to 8B parameters.
